title: 3160 manual transmission specifications
introduction:
Use this reference for the 3160 manual transmission. I start with the material specification, then check whether the transmission has a cooler before choosing its capacity row. The remaining tables give transmission weight and gear ratios—the gearbox’s leverage menu, showing how each gear trades turning force for road speed.

Match product names, part numbers and material specifications together. This page supplies reference values; application points, filling and level-check conditions, and transmission support or removal belong to the matching service procedure.

edits.text: Specified lubricants, fluids, sealers and adhesives
edits.why: Read across each row to match the named product with its part number and material specification. The fluid’s automatic-transmission product name can look surprising on a manual-gearbox page; keep the specified product tied to this transmission application.
Choose the row that matches whether the transmission has a cooler. Each capacity is expressed in quarts and liters, so keep the unit attached to the value when planning the fluid supply.
The weight row gives the same transmission mass in pounds and kilograms. I check the unit before using that figure for handling plans.

Find the selected gear in the left column, then read its ratio alongside it. Larger numerical ratios provide more torque multiplication; smaller ratios permit more road speed for a given engine speed with the rest of the driveline unchanged.

editorialRevision.scope: Only inferred engine application phrase replaced with explicit primary 3160 transmission identity. Complete 26 source units, full table/raw/context, author/independent review and final prose read; no illustrations supplied. All technical fields unchanged.
